clue.text: One said to be planting tree

indicators.note: said to be tells us the word for one who is planting is only heard, and a different spelling goes in the grid

parts.note: one planting seed is a seeder, read with the leading One

explanation.surface: Somebody is reported to be putting in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' and 'planting' together give SEEDER, someone who sows; 'said to be' says that word is only heard, and CEDAR sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a tall evergreen conifer, a familiar kind of tree.

clue.text: Didactic novelist throws out risky challenges

indicators.note: throws out suggests tossing things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A preachy author dismisses dangerous dares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws out' scrambles RISKY CHALLENGES into the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author of The Water-Babies and Westward Ho! wrote moralising, preaching fiction.

clue.text: Correct code, in the context of PC?

definitions.text: Correct code, in the context of PC?

parts.words: Correct code, in the context of PC?
parts.note: PC suggests political correctness, but in personal computing fixing faulty program code means removing the insects

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as proper language rules under political correctness.
explanation.walkthrough: PC could be political correctness (a 'correct code' of speech) or personal computer, where correcting code means removing bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove errors from computer software is to strip out its glitches.

clue.text: Start to rail at what will be charged for food

indicators.note: start to picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
ions are particles that carry an electric charge

explanation.surface: A diner begins complaining about what the bill will say for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests a bill, but means electrically charged: IONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of provisions, so the word stands for food.

clue.text: How one might describe mime about Scots town

parts.note: mime is performance without speech, so it might be described as dumb art
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a way to characterise mime with reference to a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: DUMB ART is a playful description of mime, silent theatre; ON (about) follows to complete the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a historic town on the Clyde in west-central Scotland.

clue.text: Judgement raised spirits

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: mood means spirits, state of mind

explanation.surface: A verdict lifted everyone's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' turns MOOD upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is a judgement or sentence, as in the Day of Doom.

clue.text: Faithful worker who has regular position

definitions.meaning: someone sent abroad to spread religious faith
a jokey reference to the conventional face-to-face lovemaking position named after such a worker

explanation.surface: A loyal employee holds a steady job.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the so-called missionary position, the conventional sexual position.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sent to convert others is a religious envoy, and the standard sex position bears the same name.

clue.text: Worker taking a second to drink almost all of infusion

indicators.note: second to picks out the second letter of the following word
almost all of means the final letter of the infusion is dropped

parts.note: a tisane is a herbal tea, an infusion

explanation.surface: An employee pauses briefly to sip most of a herbal tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a second' looks like a moment, but 'second to drink' is the R of drink; TISANE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual craftsman, a type of worker.

clue.text: It's time to admit mistake, for violent revolutionary

indicators.note: to admit means letting the next piece into the middle of the first ones

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone urges confession of a blunder in support of an armed rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' becomes the old poetic contraction 'tis; 'to admit' lets the mistake in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrorist uses violence for political ends, an extreme revolutionary.

clue.text: Rearranged fixture list, a number of spectators admitted, is a set that needs trying

indicators.note: admitted means the crowd figure is let into the middle of the list

parts.note: a rearranged fixture list is a new calendar of matches
a gate is the number of paying spectators at a match

explanation.surface: A revised sports schedule and the attendance figure are part of something awaiting trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Newgate Calendar recorded crimes of inmates of Newgate, London's old prison, hence a set of people needing trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Newgate Calendar was a published record of notorious criminals held in Newgate prison, people awaiting the courts.

clue.text: Great hole potentially a disaster if one's damaged at sea

definitions.meaning: in golf a hole played in three under par is a celebrated feat with this bird's name

definitions.text: potentially a disaster if one's damaged at sea
definitions.meaning: in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, shooting this seabird brings a curse on the ship

explanation.surface: A golfer's superb hole could turn into catastrophe if something is harmed out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, where killing the seabird dooms the crew; hence also a burden 'round one's neck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf names a score three under par after the large seabird, which in Coleridge's poem brings ruin on sailors who kill it.

clue.text: Three leaders leaving airport project

indicators.note: the three leading letters of the word for the airport go away, leaving the rest

parts.note: Heathrow is London's main airport

explanation.surface: Three bosses depart from an airport scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three leaders leaving' removes HEA, the first three letters of HEATHROW, London's biggest airport.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to hurl or cast it forward, as with a ball.

clue.text: Host, say, welcomed in celebrity

indicators.note: welcomed in means one piece is taken inside the other, like a guest inside a house

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: An entertainer, for instance, is received inside a famous person's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party-giver but means a great crowd, as in 'a host of angels'.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a vast number, as in a host of angels, and a legion is likewise a multitude.

clue.text: People scattered as airman entered in horrific raid

indicators.note: entered in means these pieces go inside the jumbled word that follows
horrific suggests something mangled, so the letters of raid are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PO is a pilot officer, a junior RAF airman

explanation.surface: Civilians fled as a pilot took part in a terrible bombing attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrific' jumbles the letters of raid to DIRA, and 'entered in' places the inserted pieces between its second and third letters; PO stands for pilot officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a population dispersed from its homeland, such as the Jewish dispersal.

clue.text: In brief farce, a small sum agreed with creditors

indicators.note: in means the sum is placed inside the shortened word
brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a farce is a kind of comedy
a pound is a modest sum of money

explanation.surface: Within a short comic play, a debtor settles a little money with lenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the farce word, leaving COMED, and 'In' places the sum inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To compound with creditors is to settle a debt by agreeing to pay part of it.

clue.text: The lightest material one's pen can produce?

definitions.text: The lightest material one's pen can produce?

parts.words: The lightest material one's pen can produce?
parts.note: pen reads as a writing tool, but a pen is a female swan, whose soft underplumage is very light

explanation.surface: A writer wonders what the most delicate thing their pen could create is.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan; the down it grows is a famously light, soft material.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine underfeathers of a swan were used for powder puffs and trimmings, among the lightest of fabrics.

clue.text: Ridiculously, he scorns a retired woman

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests something absurd, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man absurdly sneers at a lady who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests a pensioner, but means withdrawn from the world; HE SCORNS A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoress was a female religious recluse who withdrew from society, often walled into a cell.

clue.text: Rumour from informer first person's been arrested?

indicators.note: has been arrested means held inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Gossip from a grass that someone like me has been taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first person's' is I has, and 'been arrested' puts I inside NOSE, slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise in the old sense is talk or report spread about, as in noised abroad.

clue.text: One body of students holds copyright for part of sound system

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: holds means the student body contains the next piece

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
C is the copyright symbol's letter

explanation.surface: A student union keeps the rights to a piece of hi-fi equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound system' suggests hi-fi but means the ear; NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, or anvil, is one of the three small bones of the middle ear, which carries sound.

clue.text: The search for facts may also be a sort of fiction

definitions.meaning: systematic study of the natural world to establish knowledge

definitions.text: may also be a sort of fiction
definitions.meaning: with fiction added it names a genre of futuristic stories

explanation.surface: Seeking truth can also be a kind of storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic enquiry into nature is one sense; sci-fi, the futuristic literary genre, is the other.

clue.text: Partner failing to secure business on the other side

indicators.note: to secure means the jumbled letters close round the next piece
failing suggests the partner going wrong, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A partner proves unable to win a deal for the opposing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges the letters of Partner into PERNTRA, and 'to secure' wraps that round the business abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Per contra is a Latin phrase meaning on the contrary or on the opposite side of an account.

clue.text: Amateur at first missing Book. One had to offer too much

indicators.note: at first missing means the opening letter of the word for amateur is removed

parts.note: a lover of something is an amateur, one who does it for love
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A novice who skipped volume one ended up paying over the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first missing' removes L from LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbid is to make a bid higher than needed, as at auction or bridge.

clue.text: Such a revolution, some gunmen's twelfth

definitions.meaning: the bloodless 1688 overthrow of James II in England bears this epithet
12 August, opening of grouse shooting in Britain, is called this by those who shoot

explanation.surface: A coup is described, and armed men mark the twelfth of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when British grouse shooting begins; 'gunmen' are sporting shooters, not criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: History calls 1688's change of monarch the Glorious Revolution, and the grouse season opens on the Glorious Twelfth.

clue.text: Small pastry that may be enjoyed in cinema

definitions.text: that may be enjoyed in cinema

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A little tart is something to eat at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a snack bought at the cinema; the definition is a tearjerker film.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearjerker film, a sentimental movie that makes audiences cry, is enjoyed on screen.

clue.text: Hock is about right as basis for cocktail

indicators.note: is about means the word for hock surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to hock is to pawn something

explanation.surface: A German white wine is proper as the foundation of a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' looks like the wine but means pawn; 'cocktail' is the starter of seafood in sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The prawn cocktail, shellfish in pink sauce, is a classic British starter built on this crustacean.

clue.text: Get very hot, entering a fight

indicators.note: entering means the next piece goes inside the word for getting very hot

parts.note: to fry is to become very hot, as in the sun

explanation.surface: Someone becomes heated on joining a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts A inside FRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or brawl, as in joining the fray.

clue.text: Still be in bed about one, right?

indicators.note: about means the word for a right goes round the next piece

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is fine to remain in bed at around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about one' looks like a time but means LIEN placed round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is staying in bed late in the morning beyond the usual time.

clue.text: The last thing you want here in the pub is a double

definitions.text: The last thing you want here in the pub is a double

parts.words: The last thing you want here in the pub is a double
parts.note: sounds like turning down a large drink, but darts players must finish a game on a double ring

explanation.surface: A drinker says a large measure is the final thing wanted in this bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts, the winning throw must land in the double ring, so the final target sought at the pub board is a double.
explanation.definitionFit: The board players throw at in pub darts has a double ring that must be hit to finish.

clue.text: Beatles' hit, some time ago

definitions.meaning: a 1965 Paul McCartney ballad recorded by the Beatles
the day before today, or loosely the recent past

explanation.surface: A Liverpool band's chart song dates from a while back.
explanation.definitionFit: McCartney's much-covered Beatles song shares its title with the word for the previous day, the past.

clue.text: Assume resistance, engaging old contributor

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the first pieces hold the next one

parts.note: to don is to put on or assume, as a garment or role
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone takes on opposition by hiring an elderly giver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' gives DON, 'resistance' R; 'engaging' puts O between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives money or organs, a contributor to a cause.
